title: Friday the 13th: The Game

engine.name: Unreal Engine 4
engine.evidence: UE4 layout (Engine/Binaries, Engine/Config, Engine/Extras, SummerCamp/Content, SummerCamp/Binaries/Win64/SummerCamp.exe, Saved/), .pak content, crashpad handlers.
engine.notes: UE4 itself is offline-capable; the preservation question is the backend the game used for profiles, progression and matchmaking.

userState.role: engine config, logs and local save data

dependencies.endpoint: not statically resolvable: the executable links only Windows networking DLLs (WS2_32, WINHTTP) and the service is shut down
dependencies.evidence: official end of service 2024-12-31; no dedicated server binary in the depots
dependencies.notes: A fan revival (Friday the 13th: Resurrected) was halted by a cease-and-desist in 2024. No lawful backend exists to implement against.

dependencies.endpoint: EAC service (EasyAntiCheat/ ships in the install root)
dependencies.notes: Anti-cheat is not bypassed by this program. It also means unofficial multiplayer workarounds are out of scope.

staticAnalysis.method: PE header/import parse plus ASCII string scan of SummerCamp.exe and install-tree inventory
staticAnalysis.limits: UE4 encrypts .pak content and most service configuration lives in data, so the static picture is incomplete. Offline modes (bots, challenges, virtual cabin) exist in the shipped build and need a measured launch.

notes: Preserved surface is the offline suite; multiplayer cannot be restored without a backend that no longer exists and that this project will not fabricate around an anti-cheat.
